name: Cedarline Apparel Supply
location: Fictional operating unit in Issaquah, Washington, serving US reseller accounts.
operations: Cedarline Apparel Supply is a fictional analogue of SanMar Corporation. SanMar supplies wholesale imprintable apparel and accessories to reseller businesses and provides customer marketing resources. Its June 2025 statement describes an Issaquah headquarters and nationwide distribution. The modeled unit is an ongoing US reseller account-development desk covering customer qualification, assortment recommendations, order-service coordination, customer enablement and acquisition performance. Synthetic scale: four desk workers serve 160 active reseller businesses and 60 prospects or dormant accounts. Ordinary monthly workload includes approximately 35 qualification inquiries, 50 assortment or quotation requests, 45 order-service exceptions and eight marketing-material refreshes; the portfolio generates approximately 400 orders processed by central operations. The workspace contains 18 months of account, order and service history and six months of completed acquisition campaigns. Central credit, sales-policy administration, purchasing, warehousing and transportation remain surrounding functions. The desk produces supported commercial recommendations and processing instructions; physical fulfillment remains outside the modeled desk.

evidence.text: SanMar Corporation supplies wholesale imprintable clothing and accessories in the United States, supporting the Wholesale Trade classification.
evidence.quote: supplier of wholesale imprintable clothing and accessories in the United States
evidence.basis: The supplied captured page's About SanMar paragraph identifies SanMar Corporation and its wholesale product operation. It does not establish internal reporting relationships. The page heading and body differ by one day, so this dossier refers to the June 2025 statement.

evidence.text: The June 2025 company statement places SanMar in Issaquah, Washington, and reports nine distribution centers nationwide.
evidence.quote: SanMar is based in Issaquah, Washington, with nine distribution centers nationwide
evidence.basis: This literal passage was also revisited through the frozen-source reader. The footprint is a dated company statement, not a verified September 2026 count.

evidence.text: SanMar's June 2025 statement describes more than 50 years of business history.
evidence.quote: It all started more than 50 years ago
evidence.basis: The captured About SanMar paragraph supports the stated historical duration without establishing a precise founding date.

evidence.basis: The complete supplied paragraph contains both the referral instruction and the representative restrictions. This is a boundary for the modeled desk, not evidence of its reporting line.

evidence.basis: The supplied section 17 capture also states the order channels and that shipment of Goods is subject to availability. This supports reconciliation and qualified instructions without guaranteeing fulfillment.

evidence.basis: Versioned scenario instructions govern commitments and budgets. Credit approval, policy exceptions, account termination, customer acceptance and fulfillment remain separate decisions.

workers.responsibility: Receives the business objective, develops the working plan, supervises wholesale sales work, challenges competing assessments and accepts a coherent account-development or acquisition decision. Maintains continuing service priorities across the portfolio.
information_access: Internal desk capacity and spending authority
Specialist findings supplied through normal correspondence
workers.authority: Approves internal desk recommendations, priorities and spending allocations within supplied authority. Cannot waive brand rules, grant credit, terminate accounts or certify fulfillment. Refers policy questions through the designated route.

workers.title: Wholesale Account Representative
workers.responsibility: Assesses reseller business models, customer demand and product opportunities; reconstructs customer requests; compares commercially useful assortment options; prepares account plans and customer correspondence informed by service and marketing findings.
information_access: Customer relationship records, opportunities and communication history
Versioned product and scenario price references
Personal eligibility notes and reseller correspondence
workers.authority: Recommends products and proposed commercial terms within documented guidance. Maintains relationship records and drafts communications. Cannot treat a proposal as acceptance or negotiate sales-policy exceptions.

workers.title: Order Services Coordinator
workers.responsibility: Reconciles requested styles, variants and quantities with recorded orders, cancellations, returns and credits. Establishes documentary account prerequisites and supported order instructions. Separates actual ordering behavior from duplicate inquiries and uncompleted transactions.
information_access: Order-line, invoice, return and credit exports
Personal reconciliation workbooks and unresolved exception notes
workers.authority: Corrects desk service records and prepares line-specific processing instructions. Does not post inventory movements, grant credit or represent a requested cancellation as approved.

workers.title: Reseller Marketing and Acquisition Specialist
workers.responsibility: Analyzes acquisition cohorts and campaign economics, assesses audience and message fit, and prepares reseller-facing product content from approved materials. Connects marketing results to qualified accounts and ordering outcomes while distinguishing attribution from causation.
information_access: Campaign, ad set, ad, creative and audience records
Application-source mappings and historical acquisition metrics
Personal attribution workpapers and campaign planning files
workers.authority: Maintains campaign planning records and makes documented budget or pause changes within approved authority. Produces content revisions and recommendations; cannot invent platform approvals, customer eligibility or future conversions.

outlines.title: Choose acquisition spending that produces usable reseller relationships
outlines.objective: Assess the existing campaigns, compare at least two materially different feasible support scopes, and choose an allocation or reasoned pause. Align campaign records and account follow-up with the decision, including specific reconsideration conditions for declined support.
outlines.decision_problem: Low platform cost per result may conceal end-user inquiries, repeat contacts from existing businesses, incomplete applications or accounts that never produce usable orders. Other campaigns may produce fewer but better-qualified opportunities while requiring more sales and service effort. The marketing specialist reconstructs comparable cohorts and spending; the representative assesses business fit and realistic opportunities; the order coordinator establishes documentary readiness and net ordering outcomes. Their findings change the supervisor's support, spending and capacity decision. Compare materially different feasible allocations, including a pause where justified, while protecting existing application and service obligations. Account for concentrated buyer outcomes and distinguish historical associations from expected future returns. The accepted decision drives campaign budget and pause records, a reproducible economic comparison, customer relationship management follow-up and explicit reconsideration conditions for unsupported campaigns. Finish from recorded history without waiting for new leads or ad delivery.

outlines.title: Define a supportable assortment for a reseller's proposed selling channels
outlines.objective: Assess every proposed product and channel combination, prepare commercially useful alternatives, preserve accepted commitments and produce consistent account, order and marketing instructions.
outlines.decision_problem: A reseller's expansion combines products, decoration plans and sales channels. General account qualification does not establish that every requested combination is supportable. The representative establishes the customer need and assesses commercially suitable substitutes; the order coordinator reconciles variants, quantities, documentary prerequisites and accepted versus proposed commitments; the marketing specialist prepares product descriptions and an asset handoff that accurately reflect the supported assortment and supplied usage permissions. The supervisor selects supported opportunities, narrower proposals and scoped policy referrals. The resulting account plan drives customer relationship management opportunity records, line-specific processing instructions and revised customer materials. Every line requires a disposition; a blanket hold cannot replace the analysis. Supported substitution and scoped referral are legitimate alternatives, and an existing accepted order remains intact without evidenced amendment authority. Any storage constraint concerns a reproducible media-handoff plan, not required binary copying. Policy exceptions and customer acceptance remain outside this desk cycle.

outlines.title: Decide how to develop accounts with weakening repeat business
outlines.objective: Choose differentiated account-development responses based on the causes and commercial consequences of weak repeat purchasing.
outlines.decision_problem: A sales decline can reflect seasonal buying, misleading campaign expectations, incomplete product fit, service failures or a genuine reduction in the reseller's business. Gross order totals alone cannot distinguish these explanations. The order coordinator reconstructs net purchases, cancellations, returns and service episodes; the representative assesses recorded customer demand and the value of alternative assortments; the marketing specialist tests whether previously supplied content and acquisition messages attracted the intended businesses or created unsupported expectations. The supervisor selects justified account interventions and effort levels, weighing commercial benefit against continuing service needs and uncertain recovery. Worker findings change account plans, customer response drafts, product-resource guidance and customer relationship management obligations. The cycle preserves unresolved causes and does not claim that revised materials or follow-up have already restored sales.

assumptions: Cedarline Apparel Supply is fictional. Its desk roster, reporting relationships, account counts, workload, campaign history and authority limits are scenario assumptions, not SanMar facts.

The continuing portfolio includes 160 active reseller accounts and 60 prospects. Preserve 18 months of account, transaction and service history and six months of acquisition history. Include ordinary successful work, recurring commitments, dormant relationships and unresolved work.

The sales supervisor sets priorities and approves internal recommendations within documented authority. Staff own their working evidence and share relevant findings with colleagues when needed. Do not preassign a final task or delegation sequence.

Each employee has a distinct identity and a personal desktop, mailbox and private conversations. Common policies, meeting calendars and shared documents are available to the appropriate team; private correspondence and working notes remain with their owner.

The supervisor uses shared communications and reviewed management summaries. The account representative operates the relationship system and holds application evidence and account notes. The order coordinator works from transaction exports and service records. The marketing specialist operates campaign records and owns attribution workpapers. Grant domain applications to their ordinary operators; handoffs and approvals connect their work.

Product and price references have explicit effective dates and version histories. Earlier correspondence follows the version in force at the time. Material facts, amounts, account IDs, product IDs and dates agree across records and files.
Campaign, application, account and transaction references are joined explicitly using stable identifiers. Do not assume an automatic Meta-to-HubSpot or Drive-to-Docs integration.

Historical marketing metrics remain observations. Do not require future auctions, new customer responses, physical inspection, shipment or clock acceleration. External correspondence can remain an internally accepted unsent draft.
Sales-policy questions follow the captured referral boundary. The desk cannot negotiate pricing-policy compliance or infer exception authority from a sales title.

Central operations remains responsible for order acceptance, credit release, inventory reservation, transaction posting and physical fulfillment. The desk uses historical exports and prepares precise processing handoffs. Distinguish proposed action, existing authorization and completed processing.

Shared policies state ordinary business requirements in plain language. Personal desktops include drafts, older versions, unrelated work, useful exports and role-specific notes alongside current working files.
